label: copy phase, 4th output (recall_idx 3) in long sequences, input token in {3,t,j,v,u,c}
explanation: Very sparse unit (0.25% of steps). Fires only in the copy phase; never in the original phase or on the delimiter step, and never on the first copy output (recall_idx 0). Activation mass is concentrated at recall_idx 3 (69%) with recall_idx 2 next (13%), and in L=9 (66%) and L=8 (21%) sequences; t=12 alone holds 51% of the mass. It needs the fed-back input token (= original token recall_idx-1) to be one of a small set, mainly 3, t, j, v (u, c weaker); it is almost silent for o, 1, n, x. The output token being from a similar set (c, 3, v, u, j, t) also raises the rate, and the strongest examples are pairs such as j->v, t->v, 3->c, t->c. Even when position, length and token conditions all hold it fires on only about 20-35% of those steps, so some extra context-dependent factor that I did not identify is gating it. Magnitude is highest at the recall_idx 3 / L=9 position with these token pairs (top-quartile coverage 0.82 for the position+token predicate); I did not find any other magnitude modulator.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=12: 3, t, v, j; t=11: 3, t, v, j; t=13: 3, t, j, v) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: c, 3, v, j; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=3.
